# Idol Manager Persistence Audit: IMDataCore + Cosmo Save n Load Fixes

> **SNLF shutdown follow-up (2026-09-22):** SNLF 0.55.0 adds an attempt-completion barrier for Save and Exit/Main Menu, tracked third-party sidecar hooks, and isolated mod-owned payload schemas. Success, failure and cancellation are terminal outcomes. See the [integration contract](mods/Save%20n%20Load%20Fixes/docs/MOD_PERSISTENCE_API.md) and [native qualification](mods/Save%20n%20Load%20Fixes/docs/SHUTDOWN_QUALIFICATION_2026_09_22.md). This follow-up does not alter the frozen audit counts or close unrelated IMDC regression obligations.

> **Automated testing follow-up (2026-09-21):** native storage, crash/restart, repair ownership, public-read and Save & Quit suites now have an [automated runner and evidence record](mods/IM%20Data%20Core/docs/V6V3_AUTOMATED_QUALIFICATION_2026_09_21.md). These persistence tests require no visual verification. The record distinguishes passing bounded fixtures from the still-open full audit matrix.

> **Implementation follow-up (2026-09-09):** the v6/v3 loader enforces the no-migration policy and protects unsupported forward-envelope schemas from backup downgrade. Actual Unity tests also found and fixed omitted collections in Graduation Details persistence and IMDC random-event payloads. Native consumer/save/load evidence and remaining qualification work are tracked in [`V6V3_QUALIFICATION_STATUS.md`](mods/IM%20Data%20Core/docs/V6V3_QUALIFICATION_STATUS.md). Frozen audit counts remain unchanged. Historical task checkpoints below are not current release-status assertions.


> **Current storage compatibility policy (3.4.34+):** IM Data Core supports only **sidecar v6 + journal v3**. Sidecar v1-v5 and journal v1-v2 are unsupported release inputs. IMDC does **not** promise, qualify, or require in-place migration, conversion, adoption, or rewrite from those older storage generations. Encountering an unsupported older generation must fail closed without converting it or overwriting its bytes. Any v5/v2 migration language retained below is historical design/task context, not a current compatibility commitment.

**Product-policy override (2026-09-07):** frozen finding **#56** remains part of the historical audit record, but it is **retired from the current IMDataCore release obligation**. IMDC will not provide backwards compatibility from sidecar v1-v5 / journal v1-v2 into v6/v3. The current active numbered IMDataCore obligation count is therefore **58**, plus the five separate durable-identity contracts. Regression clauses whose sole purpose was pre-v6 storage migration are superseded by unsupported-generation fail-closed checks. This policy change does not alter historical audit counts; it changes the current product acceptance scope.

Unified findings from the supplied decompiled **Idol Manager** code, the supplied **Cosmo Mod Library / IM Data Core** Harmony mod, and the supplied audit chat history.

## Executive summary

This audit has **two equal deliverables**:

1. **IMDataCore coverage audit**: find missing hooks, historical/state payloads, lifecycle coverage, stable identities, and persistence behavior that other Harmony mods reasonably need from IMDataCore as Cosmo Mod Library's shared backend.
2. **Cosmo Save n Load Fixes / vanilla-fix audit**: find vanilla bugs that should be repaired by a separate Harmony mod. Save/load continuity remains the primary focus of this persistence audit, and any case where loading the same save can reconstruct material gameplay state differently, lose/duplicate state, corrupt a saved value, or resume differently is automatically in scope. The mod is **not limited to persistence bugs**: other verified vanilla bugs encountered during these audits may also be routed to Save n Load Fixes when they need patching. This keeps vanilla repair work out of IMDataCore's shared historical schema without artificially excluding worthwhile non-persistence fixes.

The two-backlog model does **not** require duplicating a vanilla repair that the supplied Cosmo tree already owns in a dedicated fix mod. When a source-matched dedicated repair already exists, this audit records that ownership explicitly, revalidates its coverage, and routes uncovered sibling surfaces to that same dedicated owner when doing so is cleaner than implementing the same transport mechanism twice. Area #10 Pass E applies this rule to **Save Write Ordering Fix 1.3.0**.

**Post-audit implementation decision:** defect accounting remains unchanged, but **Save n Load Fixes will embed its own Mono-safe ordered save/read transport** so the new repair mod has no runtime dependency on standalone Save Write Ordering Fix. Standalone SWOF remains a separately shippable implementation of the same one transport family and will be extended for `GlobalData`. When both mods are installed, Save n Load Fixes is the preferred effective transport owner and standalone SWOF must recognize/delegate to it rather than double-patching or running a second queue. This is an implementation-coexistence decision, not a second transport finding.

The fifty-three IMDataCore-only numbered findings (#14-#29 and #32-#68) are **IMDataCore-only audit findings** as historical/backend omissions or event-stream correctness defects. Vanilla does not need those historical details for ordinary continuation, but diary/history consumers may reasonably want them. Findings #30 and #31 are different: each contains an IMDataCore historical/lifecycle gap **and** a separate vanilla gameplay-state defect, so both belong to both backlogs. Finding #22 also exposed a **separate** vanilla award-speech consistency bug, tracked outside the numbered history inventory under Save n Load Fixes; Area #8 Pass A independently exposed the ignored-immutable-`DateTime` graduation-date bug family, Pass B strengthened that family with two additional discarded `AddDays(...)` call sites, and Pass B exposed the separate show next-episode/cancellation-date helper bug. Those separate live bugs do not make the historical omissions themselves save/load findings. The broader Save n Load Fixes scope does **not** mean every IMDataCore history gap is automatically a vanilla bug.

Conversely, technical runtime restoration values such as `girl_paused`, `business_minutes_before_finish`, tutorial baselines, pending ambient scene jobs, and scheduler state are **Save n Load Fixes work**, not reasons to expand IMDataCore's shared historical schema.

**Post-gate rule:** this separation now applies even when a datum originally appeared in both backlogs. For #1/#2/#5/#6/#30/#31, the repair layer is the **only persistence owner of any current-state value needed for continuation**. IMDataCore must not save a duplicate copy of that repair-owned current state in its sidecar, checkpoint, bootstrap, or adoption baseline. IMDataCore keeps only independently useful historical event/context semantics that the repaired game does not need for continuation. Current-state load/adoption/query paths should read repaired vanilla directly.

### Architectural rule

IMDataCore and Save n Load Fixes may cooperate, but they own different semantics:

- **IMDataCore** owns shared hooks, mod-owned namespaced state, useful vanilla **history and coverage provenance**, stable historical identity, and sidecar/query correctness. Canonical current gameplay state remains in repaired vanilla.
- **Save n Load Fixes** owns verified vanilla bug repair by default. Save/load continuation, reconstruction, migration compatibility, and unsafe save boundaries are its primary audit focus, but they are not a hard scope ceiling.
- **Existing dedicated vanilla-fix mods normally remain the implementation owner when the supplied Cosmo tree already contains a narrower source-matched repair and duplicating it would create competing patches.** The post-audit Save n Load Fixes plan makes one explicit infrastructure exception for the ordered save/read transport: SNLF embeds a compatible implementation so it has no SWOF dependency, while standalone SWOF remains separately maintained and yields to SNLF when both are active. This changes implementation topology, not defect accounting or semantic ownership.
- If Save n Load Fixes needs supplemental persistence for a value vanilla omitted, that state should be owned by the Save n Load Fixes mod. It may use IMDataCore's namespaced mod-state API as infrastructure if desired, but it should **not** be smuggled into IMDataCore's shared historical event schema merely to repair vanilla.
- If vanilla already saved enough information, Save n Load Fixes should repair/reconstruct from that information rather than duplicating it.
- IMDataCore recording a useful historical fact does **not** make IMDataCore responsible for writing it back into vanilla runtime state.
- **Repaired vanilla is the canonical source for current gameplay state, and repair-owned current state has exactly one persistence owner.** Once Save n Load Fixes or a narrower dedicated repair persists/restores a value needed for continuation, IMDataCore must **not save another copy of that current value at all**: not as restoration state, not as a checkpoint mirror, not as a bootstrap fallback, and not as an adoption/baseline value. If IMDataCore needs the current value after load, it reads/infers it from the repaired vanilla runtime.
- IMDataCore may still store a **coverage-horizon marker** saying when historical observation began, but that marker must not duplicate repair-owned current gameplay values. Adoption may capture only independently historical facts that are not being persisted by the repair layer as continuation state.
- If a repaired value later changes or is overwritten in normal play, IMDataCore may still need a distinct earlier **historical occurrence** in history. That is the key distinction between **duplicate current-state persistence (reject)** and **historical event/context capture (retain)**.

## Audit mission, ownership, and boundary

The supplied IMDataCore documentation describes IMDC as the **shared persistence and historical-event backend used by Cosmo Idol Manager mods**. It exposes namespaced custom JSON, timeline events, money-ledger queries, explicit flush, physical-save identity, and persistence diagnostics, while keeping that data in a sidecar rather than modifying vanilla save JSON.

For this audit, IMDataCore's mission is interpreted narrowly and intentionally. The design preference is to keep vanilla save data focused on what the game itself needs to operate, while richer optional historical/mod data lives in IMDataCore's sidecar. When vanilla needs repair, that repair belongs in **Cosmo Save n Load Fixes** rather than silently redefining IMDataCore as the game's second save format.

The audit therefore produces **two implementation backlogs from the same source investigation**. A finding can be routed to IMDataCore, Save n Load Fixes, both, or neither. Save n Load Fixes is the project's **vanilla bug-fix mod**, despite its persistence-oriented name. A save/load divergence is automatically relevant, and other verified vanilla bugs encountered during any audit area may also be added. "Not an IMDataCore gap" never means "not worth fixing"; it may instead be a direct vanilla repair item.

### In scope for IMDataCore

- durable mod-owned custom state;
- useful vanilla historical facts that disappear from vanilla data;
- useful **historical** baselines for facts not already persisted as repair-owned current gameplay state, plus coverage-horizon metadata that tells consumers when IMDataCore observation began;
- stable entity identity and occurrence correlation for historical rows;
- event lifecycle symmetry and payload semantics;
- reliable hooks/capture points needed to support the above;
- exact association of sidecar state/history with the correct physical vanilla save/branch.

### Not automatically an IMDataCore responsibility

- repairing vanilla runtime state after load;
- turning the sidecar into a second complete game save;
- serializing arbitrary delegates, coroutine closures, UI queues, or every private field;
- preserving every technical scheduler/timer solely because vanilla forgot it;
- guaranteeing deterministic RNG replay;
- logging every internal operation for diagnostics or system-administrator-style tracing.


### In scope for Cosmo Save n Load Fixes

Cosmo Save n Load Fixes is the project's **vanilla repair mod**. Its name reflects the original and still-primary problem class, but it is not restricted to persistence defects.

A finding belongs in its backlog when either:

- it is a verified vanilla save/load, reconstruction, migration, serialization, save-boundary, or continuation bug; **or**
- it is another verified vanilla gameplay bug encountered during the audit that needs a Harmony patch and does not belong to IMDataCore's own implementation.

For persistence specifically, **loading the same vanilla save into materially different reconstructed gameplay state is itself a bug**, including legacy-save fallback paths that roll fresh birthdays, peak ages, fan allocations, relationship dynamics, rival populations, or other gameplay-relevant state. The fact that an old schema never stored the later field affects the repair strategy; it does not make nondeterministic reconstruction acceptable.

Preferred repair order:

1. **Fix reconstruction first** when vanilla already saved the necessary information.
2. **Derive the missing value** when it is deterministic from saved state.
3. **Make compatibility migration deterministic** when an old save genuinely lacks a newer field but the loader currently synthesizes materially different state on repeated loads. Prefer stable reconstruction from saved identity/state; otherwise keep any migration cache under repair-mod ownership.
4. **Persist only the minimal missing semantic value** when the state is genuinely non-inferable and cannot be stably reconstructed.
5. Keep repair-owned supplemental data under the Save n Load Fixes mod's ownership. If IMDataCore is used as the storage backend, use a namespaced custom-state contract rather than adding technical repair fields to IMDataCore's shared historical payloads.
6. Preserve intended vanilla gameplay as closely as possible. Fix the bug without opportunistically redesigning unrelated mechanics.

#### Legacy missing-data migration policy

When an old vanilla save row genuinely predates a field and therefore contains no authoritative value to restore, Save n Load Fixes must **not fabricate false historical certainty**, but it should also not allow the same untouched save to synthesize different gameplay state on every load.

Use this precedence order:

1. **Derive exactly from other saved state** when the missing value is recoverable.
2. **Use a canonical compatibility default** when the field's semantics make one unambiguously appropriate.
3. **Otherwise synthesize once, deterministically**, preserving vanilla's intended value domain/distribution as closely as practical. Seed or derive the result from stable saved identity, such as physical-save identity + entity identity + migration-field code + migration-version code.
4. **Do not consume or temporarily reseed `UnityEngine.Random` merely to perform migration.** Prefer an isolated deterministic PRNG or direct hash-to-value derivation so compatibility migration does not perturb the game's global future RNG stream.
5. Treat the synthesized result as **authoritative reconstructed state immediately**.
6. On the player's next ordinary save, let the modern vanilla field serialize that reconstructed value normally. That save thereby **commits the migration** and future loads no longer need the fallback.
7. If the player repeatedly loads the original untouched legacy save without resaving, the deterministic migration must reconstruct the **same synthesized values every time**.
8. Never infer “missing” from a value that is valid in the field's real domain. Prefer field presence, schema/version information, nullable representation, or an explicit migration marker. The risky-single `Marketing_Result == 0f` bug is the canonical warning against overlapping valid values with sentinels.
9. Use repair-owned supplemental migration state only when deterministic derivation is impractical. If IMDataCore provides the storage transport, keep that cache in a **Save n Load Fixes namespace** rather than shared IMDataCore historical schema.

Concrete Pass G applications:

- missing legacy idol `birthday` / `peakAge`: deterministic per saved idol, constrained to vanilla-valid semantics;
- legacy aggregate fans: deterministic redistribution that preserves the old saved aggregate total exactly;
- missing legacy relationship rows/dynamics: deterministic reconstruction keyed by stable unordered idol-pair identity while retaining vanilla's intended relationship-generation semantics;
- missing legacy rival state: deterministic generation keyed to the physical save/migration version so the same old save always receives the same migrated rival ecosystem.

The goal is not to claim we recovered a value the old format never stored. The goal is to make **migration itself stable**: the same old save has one reproducible migrated interpretation, and the next modern save records that interpretation normally.

Typical Save n Load Fixes work includes hidden room continuation fields, lost scheduler clocks, pending authoritative jobs, load-order reconstruction, unsupported Unity serialization state, loader sentinel/reinitialization bugs, nondeterministic legacy migration, unsafe save boundaries, and other verified vanilla bugs discovered while auditing.

### Not automatically a Save n Load Fixes responsibility

- preserving a historical fact solely for diary/reporting when no vanilla gameplay bug exists;
- repairing IMDataCore's own entity identity, payload, lifecycle, query, or sidecar semantics;
- logging raw RNG rolls merely because they occurred;
- guaranteeing identical **future** RNG trajectories when reconstructed gameplay state itself is identical, unless deterministic replay becomes an explicit project goal;
- intentional vanilla behavior differences that are design choices rather than defects.

A missing Harmony patch is therefore an IMDataCore issue **only when it prevents the backend/ledger from exposing useful state or history to consumers**. It is not a defect merely because a vanilla method exists and IMDC does not log it.

This README remains primarily a **persistence/history audit**, not a complete audit of every vanilla system or every IMDataCore hook/API surface. However, when the source work exposes a concrete vanilla bug outside strict persistence, it may still be recorded in the Save n Load Fixes backlog rather than discarded for being out-of-theme. Hook quality for IMDataCore is still evaluated here only where it affects persistence, historical capture, identity, or consumer query semantics.

Likewise, IMDataCore's exact-save checkpoints are treated as **sidecar branch/state anchors**. They exist so IMDC can bind its own supplemental state/history to the correct vanilla save and rewind safely. They are not interpreted as a promise that `vanilla save + IMDC sidecar` must reconstruct every omitted vanilla runtime field.

A separate future overhaul may make consumer-facing features such as an idol career diary more narrative and less technical. This persistence audit only asks whether the underlying useful facts are available and semantically trustworthy; presentation is outside scope.

## Audit criterion

The audit now applies three separate tests.

### Test A: Vanilla bug / Cosmo Save n Load Fixes routing

A finding is a **Cosmo Save n Load Fixes candidate** when source analysis establishes a vanilla defect that is appropriate to repair with the fix mod. Save/load defects are automatically included when any of the following is true:

1. vanilla saved an authoritative value but the loader restores, overwrites, duplicates, or interprets it incorrectly;
2. vanilla omits state needed to resume an already-established operation correctly;
3. loading the same serialized save can synthesize materially different gameplay state because reconstruction or compatibility fallback consumes fresh randomness;
4. a save boundary can capture only part of an authoritative operation and therefore resume from an impossible or altered state; or
5. load order, initialization, serialization, or reconstruction causes gameplay to differ from the state represented by the save.

The mod may also receive **non-persistence vanilla bugs** discovered during these audits. The information-theoretic questions "was the value saved?" and "can it be inferred?" determine the preferred repair technique, **not eligibility for the fix mod**.

`UnityEngine.Random.state` remains separate when the only difference is the future stochastic trajectory and all material reconstructed gameplay fields are otherwise the same. That is deterministic replay rather than ordinary state restoration unless the project explicitly adopts deterministic continuation.

Examples such as `Progress_Init`, the risky-marketing zero-sentinel bug, `LastGirlID`, and the legacy fallback rerandomizations show the full range: inferred values, already-saved values, loader side effects, and genuinely missing old-schema fields can all be Save n Load Fixes work.

### Test B: IMDataCore ledger/backend relevance

For this audit, **"vanilla" now means the repaired vanilla baseline when judging IMDataCore ownership**: the base game after the confirmed Save n Load Fixes repairs and any narrower dedicated vanilla-fix owner such as Save Write Ordering Fix have done their job. IMDataCore is not a fallback second save format for defects that the repair layer already makes canonical.

A datum remains an **IMDataCore ledger/backend gap** when all of the following are true:

1. the datum is reasonably useful to downstream mods for historical reconstruction, state-change history, semantic cause, occurrence correlation, durable historical identity, or another consumer-facing backend purpose;
2. after the repaired vanilla baseline is applied, the game still does **not** retain the required *historical occurrence/context/identity* for as long as consumers may need it, even if it now retains the current gameplay value needed for continuation;
3. IMDataCore currently does not capture, identify, order, or expose that historical/backend information correctly;
4. preserving it fits IMDataCore's optional sidecar role and does not require duplicating the repaired game's canonical continuation state;
5. when Save n Load Fixes or another dedicated repair owns persistence of a current gameplay value, IMDataCore must **not persist a second copy of that value at all** in shared sidecar/checkpoint/bootstrap/adoption state; current-state load, adoption, capture, and query paths must read/infer it from the repaired vanilla runtime; and
6. IMDataCore may persist a **coverage-horizon marker** and independently useful historical occurrences/context, but an adoption/baseline record must not duplicate a repair-owned current gameplay value merely for provenance or fallback.

This creates an explicit source-of-truth split:

- **current gameplay state** -> repaired vanilla runtime/save state;
- **technical repair-only continuation metadata** -> Save n Load Fixes or the narrower dedicated repair owner;
- **historical occurrences, semantic causes, and historical correlation identities** -> IMDataCore sidecar;
- **mod-owned custom state** -> the owning mod's IMDataCore namespace when it chooses IMDC as storage infrastructure.

A finding may still pass **both** Test A and Test B. In that case the two mods own different semantics. Save n Load Fixes owns persistence/restoration of the canonical current gameplay state; IMDataCore records only the distinct historical fact that remains useful after that repair. This split **never permits IMDataCore to save a second current-state copy** of a value already persisted by the repair layer.

For IMDataCore, the audit still rejects data that is merely private, transient, presentation-only, or has no plausible consumer-facing historical/backend value. For Save n Load Fixes, absence from vanilla JSON is not itself the criterion: the question is whether vanilla behavior is defective and whether the repair layer should make the loaded game state faithful to the saved checkpoint.

### Test C: persistence-ownership migration / no duplicate continuation state

Every value that IMDataCore **currently persists or is proposed to persist** must also pass a persistence-owner migration test. This test is separate from whether the datum is historically interesting.

1. Classify the persisted value by semantic role: **current vanilla continuation state**, **repair-only continuation metadata**, **historical occurrence/context**, **historical correlation identity**, **mod-owned custom state**, or **branch/identity validation witness**.
2. If the value is required so vanilla can load the same save and resume the same material gameplay state, that persistence belongs to **Cosmo Save n Load Fixes** or the narrower dedicated vanilla-repair owner. If IMDataCore currently persists such a value as a live-state mirror/checkpoint/baseline, the audit must mark an explicit **full or partial move**, name the exact IMDataCore storage field/API being removed or narrowed, name the target repair-owned field/contract, and state what IMDataCore may retain afterward.
3. A historical event may still contain the same scalar **only when its semantics are point-in-time history**, such as “this relationship occurrence had `Dynamic = negative`.” That historical row must never be used as the authoritative current-state restore source.
4. Minimal hashes, structural witnesses, or generation locators derived from vanilla may remain in IMDataCore when they exist solely to bind/validate IMDataCore history and cannot reconstruct gameplay by themselves. The checkpoint content fingerprint and agency-room generation witnesses are canonical examples.
5. IMDataCore's namespaced custom JSON API is **transport, not semantic ownership**. If Save n Load Fixes stores a repair-owned value through that API, the value must live under a Save n Load Fixes namespace/key contract and remains Save n Load Fixes-owned; it must not be promoted into IMDataCore shared historical schema.
6. If no current IMDataCore source field actually mirrors continuation state, record **zero physical moves** rather than inventing one. Planned split-responsibility findings must still say exactly which future/current-state portion belongs only in Save n Load Fixes so the duplication is not introduced later.

# Detailed findings

## 1. Relationship initial `Dynamic`

### Vanilla behavior

`Relationships._relationship.Initialize()` seeds relationship history and then establishes the dynamic:

- dating-compatible relationships become `positive`;
- other relationships randomly choose enum values 1..3, corresponding to positive/neutral/negative.

In the supplied decompile this is in `Relationships.cs`, around lines 934-946.

Weekly relationship processing later applies automatic drift:

- `positive` -> `Add(+0.1)`
- `negative` -> `Add(-0.1)`

See `Relationships.cs`, around lines 414-426.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`Relationships.GetDataForSaving()` serializes:

- girl IDs,
- `Vals`,
- `Dating`,
- `Temp`.

It does **not** serialize `Dynamic` (`Relationships.cs`, around lines 502-516).

On load, vanilla constructs a fresh `_relationship`, restores those fields, and calls `Recalc(true)` (`Relationships.cs`, around lines 563-578). The `_relationship` field initializer is:

```csharp
public Relationships._relationship._dynamic Dynamic = Relationships._relationship._dynamic.neutral;
```

Therefore a relationship that had a positive or negative dynamic can reload as neutral if nothing else re-establishes it.

### IMDataCore relevance

IMDataCore already models `relationship_dynamic` and writes it in several relationship lifecycle payloads. However, the current relationship Harmony patch set covers events such as dating, breakups, `Add`, removal, and bullying changes. It does **not** capture the initial value established by `_relationship.Initialize()`.

That is a real **ledger gap** for downstream mods that want to understand relationship evolution: a relationship can begin with a negative or positive tendency, never hit a later IMDC relationship event, and leave no sidecar record of the original tendency.

Separately, vanilla restoring the relationship as neutral is a **vanilla save/load bug**. IMDataCore does not need to repair the live game state merely because it records the original value.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** capture the **historical creation occurrence** with the initial relationship dynamic at relationship creation, keyed by a stable unordered idol-pair identity. **If Save n Load Fixes persists/restores current `Dynamic`, IMDataCore must not persist another current `Dynamic` copy anywhere in its sidecar, checkpoint, bootstrap, or adoption baseline.** After load or adoption, any IMDataCore code that needs the current value must read it from the repaired live relationship object. For an adopted pre-coverage career where the original creation occurrence is unknowable, store only a coverage-start marker; do not manufacture an `initial Dynamic` event from the current repaired value.

Useful fields include:

- idol A ID,
- idol B ID,
- `relationship_dynamic`,
- coarse relationship status,
- dating state,
- known-to-player state,
- initial `Vals`/ratio if useful.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** serialize/restore `Dynamic` correctly, or patch vanilla's relationship reconstruction. That repair should live in Cosmo Save n Load Fixes code rather than being an implicit responsibility of IMDataCore.

## 2. Random-event selected business contract

### Vanilla behavior

A normal `Event_Manager` random event can include a business requirement. During requirement-variable setup, vanilla selects one qualifying active proposal at random:

```csharp
Event_Manager.VARIABLE__BIZ_PROPOSAL =
    ExtensionMethods.GetRandomElement<business.active_proposal>(
        Business.GetActiveProposals(Girl, type));
```

See `Event_Manager.cs`, around line 329.

The pointer is subsequently used for:

- `[proposal_agent]`,
- `[proposal_product]`,
- money/effect calculations,
- terminating or breaking the selected contract.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`Event_Manager.ActiveEventData` persists event identity, state, dates, and actors. It does not contain the selected business proposal. See `Event_Manager.cs`, around lines 720-814 and the `ActiveEventData` DTO around line 1329.

If an idol has multiple qualifying active proposals, the exact randomly selected proposal is not inferable from the save.

### IMDataCore relevance

IMDataCore patches `Event_Manager.StartEvent` and captures rich random-event context, but the current source contains no `VARIABLE__BIZ_PROPOSAL` or selected-contract field in that event history.

That is useful ledger context: a downstream mod should be able to tell **which exact contract the random event referred to**, especially when several qualifying contracts existed. The patch is well positioned because its postfix runs immediately after `StartEvent`, while the selected object still exists.

Separately, vanilla losing or misbinding that selected pointer across save/load is a **vanilla save/load bug**. IMDataCore recording the contract reference does not make IMDataCore responsible for restoring the event's runtime pointer.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** add the selected contract to the random-event history using a stable **contract instance ID**, plus useful denormalized details. **After Save n Load Fixes rebinds `VARIABLE__BIZ_PROPOSAL`, IMDataCore should sample the canonical repaired vanilla pointer only when recording a real event occurrence; it must not persist/restore that runtime pointer or create an adoption baseline copy of it.** For an adopted save that is already inside an active event, keep only coverage-horizon metadata until a real post-adoption occurrence can be observed; do not manufacture a historical selection row from current repaired state.

- selected contract present,
- target idol ID,
- contract instance ID,
- contract type,
- agent name,
- product name,
- payment,
- end date,
- buzz/fans/fame/stamina terms.

This should be implemented together with the contract-identity fix described later in this README.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** persist/rebind the selected proposal in vanilla event state if correct save/load continuation is desired.

## 3. Queued substory `BeforeStart` semantic setup / actor binding

### Vanilla behavior

`Substories_Manager.StartDialogue(...)` can enqueue a dialogue together with an `Action BeforeStart` callback. The queue entry stores:

```csharp
public Action BeforeStart;
```

When the dialogue actually becomes runnable, `_CheckDialogueQueue` invokes `BeforeStart()` immediately before activating the dialogue.

See `Substories_Manager.cs`, around lines 98-145, 774-790, and the queue consumer around lines 980-992.

### Vanilla persistence hole

The vanilla queue DTO stores the dialogue ID, launch time, delay, and debug flag. `GetDialogueQueueForLoading()` reconstructs those fields but no callback. The queue save/load logic is around `Substories_Manager.cs` lines 595-629.

A queued substory can therefore survive a save while the callback that was supposed to run immediately before it is silently discarded.

Area #2 Pass C tightened the original description by source-enumerating the supplied vanilla call sites instead of treating `Action` as an abstract worst case. There are **13 direct non-null `BeforeStart` scheduling call sites** in the supplied root source: one in `Event_Overlord` and twelve in `Dating`. Their concrete uses are mostly **semantic actor binding plus date/scene presentation setup**, not arbitrary unrelated gameplay mutation.

Examples include:

- the `agnostic` event binding the already-selected center idol into the substory actor slot before the dialogue starts;
- generic/public/private date flows binding the exact participating idol and preparing the corresponding date sprite/scene state;
- `date_fujimoto_warning` binding the idol identified by `Dating.Data.Caught_GirlID`;
- `date_friend` binding the current partner plus the selected best friend;
- `date_ex` binding the current partner plus the selected ex-partner.

The generic API can still carry an arbitrary `Action`, but the supplied vanilla source supports a narrower and more actionable repair statement: **the queued dialogue row is durable while its required semantic pre-start binding/setup is not**. The callback cannot be reconstructed from the saved boolean alone, and dialogue ID by itself is not always sufficient to recover the exact actor object selected when the callback was created.

### IMDataCore relevance

IMDataCore's `Substories_Manager.StartDialogue` patch receives the callback and records:

```text
had_before_start_callback = beforeStart != null
```

Under the clarified scope, this is **not a core IMDataCore persistence gap**. An `Action` delegate is technical runtime machinery, not a sensible historical-ledger object. IMDC should not become responsible for serializing closures merely because vanilla fails to preserve their semantic setup.

There is still a useful backend opportunity: cooperating mods may benefit from a semantic hook/registry for known pre-start action codes and JSON arguments. That should remain explicit and opt-in rather than a generic delegate serializer.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** keep the existing boolean as lightweight metadata. If real consumer demand exists, add a semantic registration API where vanilla/mod call sites can provide an action code plus stable arguments. Do not snapshot opaque delegates or coroutine closure state.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** restore the concrete queued-dialogue pre-start semantics from a small semantic descriptor attached to the durable queue row: setup kind plus the stable idol/actor IDs and source-specific arguments needed by the source-verified vanilla call site. Correlate the descriptor to the saved queue occurrence using queue order plus dialogue ID / launch-time witnesses, then rebuild a fresh runtime callback after load. Do not serialize the delegate object itself, and do not invent a universal migration for old rows whose exact actor/setup semantics cannot be derived.

---

## 4. Active room `substoryScene` identity

### Vanilla behavior

A substory scene assigns a dialogue object directly to a room:

```csharp
this.substoryScene = _dialogue;
this.status = agency._room._status.substoryScene;
```

`DrawSpriteScene()` later dereferences `substoryScene` to resolve the prefab and initialize the `Scene_Container`.

See `agency.cs`, around lines 3288-3314.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`agency.GetRoomDataForSaving()` serializes room `status` plus many actor/project/timer fields, but it does **not** serialize `substoryScene` or its dialogue ID. The field exists only on `_room` (`agency.cs`, around line 3828).

On load the room status is restored from `RoomData`, so a room can be recreated with `status == substoryScene` while `substoryScene == null`.

That is an authoritative object identity that cannot be derived from the room status alone.

### IMDataCore relevance

IMDataCore preserves durable room-generation identity for historical correlation, which is exactly within its mission. The missing live `substoryScene` pointer, however, is a **vanilla runtime reconstruction problem**, not a core sidecar-ledger requirement.

Historical substory/scene events can still be recorded normally. IMDataCore does not need to mirror the active room's technical dialogue pointer merely to make vanilla resume correctly.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** no built-in persistence change is required solely for this runtime pointer. If downstream mods need to observe room-scene activation, a semantic hook/event is preferable to checkpointing the object reference.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** persist/rebind the active substory dialogue identity in vanilla-compatible room load logic so `status == substoryScene` cannot reconstruct with a null dialogue.

---

## 5. Show last-episode `FanAppeal`

### Vanilla behavior

`Shows._show.NewEpisode()` calls `UpdateCast()`, which calls `RecalcFanAppeal()`, then the resulting appeal ratios feed audience/opinion and other episode calculations.

The `_show` object keeps:

```csharp
public List<singles._fanAppeal> FanAppeal
```

See `Shows.cs`, around lines 1516-1599 and field declaration around line 2195.

`Cancel()` also consults the stored `FanAppeal` to determine which fan group is most disappointed when a sufficiently established show is cancelled (`Shows.cs`, around lines 1982-2006).

### Vanilla persistence hole

`Shows.GetDataForSaving()` serializes show identity/status, history arrays, parameters, cast, cancellation state, etc., but does not serialize `FanAppeal` (`Shows.cs`, around lines 552-585).

After load, the exact ratios from the last completed episode are therefore gone.

They are not always exactly reconstructible from the present-day save because appeal depends on the cast and game state at the time the episode was calculated, and those inputs may have changed since that episode.

### IMDataCore status

The current IMDataCore source is slightly better than the older shorthand in the chat history:

- `show_episode_released` **does** record the episode cast ID list;
- configuration-change events can carry `show_fan_appeal_summary_before/after`;
- but `ShowEpisodePayload` itself does **not** carry the exact per-episode fan-appeal ratios.

So the current gap should be described specifically as **last-episode FanAppeal**, not as a total lack of per-episode cast history.

### IMDataCore relevance

This is a **core historical payload gap** because exact episode appeal is useful to mods reconstructing show history, audience context, or an idol's career record. IMDataCore already has a natural `show_episode_released` event on which to store it.

The fact that vanilla may later use the lost appeal for cancellation/opinion behavior is a separate vanilla save/load problem. IMDataCore does not need to feed the value back into the live show object.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** extend `ShowEpisodePayload` with a deterministic fan-appeal summary for the completed episode, ideally the same canonical representation already used by show configuration events. **Once Save n Load Fixes restores the show's live last-episode `FanAppeal`, that repaired vanilla field is the current-state authority.** IMDataCore should read it when capturing/querying/adopting and preserve appeal only as per-episode history; it should not maintain a competing sidecar value for restoring the show.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** if exact post-load show behavior depends on the last episode's appeal, vanilla-compatible save/load code should persist/reconstruct that runtime field directly.

---

## 6. `Event_Templates.Active_Template` save bug + missing template-event history

### Vanilla behavior

Idol Manager has a second random-event mechanism in `Event_Templates` in addition to `Event_Manager`.

`Event_Templates.StartRandomEvent()` creates `Active_Template` and randomly determines, among other things:

- template,
- idol/staff/NPC actors,
- generated names/gender,
- accepted random template parts,
- random part values,
- available replies,
- local variables,
- internal `Damage`.

Actor/part actions can also mutate career state before the popup is eventually presented.

### Cross-save window

After selection, the popup is opened through coroutine scheduling. There is therefore a legitimate interval in which `Active_Template` is fully selected but not yet consumed by the popup.

The audit history additionally established that vanilla's autosave guard does not explicitly test `Event_Templates.Active_Template`, and F5 manual save bypasses the normal autosave eligibility check anyway.

### Vanilla persistence hole

There is no `Event_Templates` state in vanilla `SavedData`. A load destroys:

- selected template,
- selected actors,
- selected parts/values,
- reply set,
- template-local variables,
- `Damage`,
- the pending coroutine.

Because the selections are random, the lost event is not reconstructible exactly.

### IMDataCore relevance

The current IMDataCore source has no semantic `Event_Templates` lifecycle capture. Its `random_event_started` / `random_event_concluded` events patch the separate `Event_Manager` system.

That is a **core historical lifecycle gap** because `Event_Templates` produces player-visible gameplay events and consequences that downstream diary/history mods may reasonably need. However, the historical requirement is **not the same thing as serializing the entire pending `Active_Template` object so vanilla can resume it**.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** model useful template-event history with a lifecycle such as the following. The Track-B gate specifically rejects an IMDC-owned pending-`Active_Template` restoration record: repaired saves should not cross the selected-to-popup unsafe boundary, and while the event is live IMDataCore can observe the vanilla object directly.

- `template_event_presented`;
- `template_event_concluded`;
- optionally `template_event_selected` when selection-time context or pre-presentation effects are historically meaningful.

Payloads should preserve the event identity, relevant actors, selected parts/values, reply/outcome identity, and any semantic consequences needed by consumers. Avoid dumping every internal field merely because it exists.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** make the selected-to-popup handoff non-checkpointable instead of serializing the rich `Active_Template` composite. Set a narrow repair-owned pending-open blocker once template selection succeeds and `_OpenPopup()` is scheduled, and clear it only when the random-event popup actually opens; the same blocker must cover manual save and in-game load as well as autosave. Do **not** use `Active_Template != null` as the blocker, because the supplied source does not clear that static field on ordinary conclusion. A pre-fix save already captured inside this handoff has no generally safe reconstruction contract from vanilla data alone.

---

## 7. `Activities.Chain`

### Vanilla behavior

`Activities.Chain` stores the remaining ordered activity queue. The chain progression coroutine consumes `Chain[0]` and then removes it.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`Activities.Awake()` clears `Activities.Chain`.

`Activities.SaveFunction()` saves current activity timing/lock state and the activity data list, but not `Activities.Chain` (`Activities.cs`, around lines 1262-1327 and field declaration around line 1377).

Therefore a future plan such as:

```text
Spa -> Promotion -> Performance -> Spa
```

can lose all remaining queued intent after reload.

The queue order cannot be inferred from completed activity history or player resources because it represents future intent.

### IMDataCore relevance

IMDataCore records activity outcomes but does not persist the player's remaining future-action queue.

Under the clarified scope, this is **not a core IMDataCore persistence requirement**. `Activities.Chain` is player intent and vanilla runtime scheduling state, not historical ledger data. A mod that specifically wants automation-plan persistence can own that state through IMDC's custom-data API.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** no built-in chain snapshot is required.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** persist the ordered `Activities.Chain` enum list as repair-owned state. No extra coroutine/phase token is needed: `Chain_Progress_Do()` removes the head only after dispatch, so a restored head remains authoritative and vanilla timing can dispatch it when due. On F9, invalidate any discarded pre-load chain iterator before restoring the target chain so the loaded head cannot be dispatched twice.

---

## 8. `Event_Overlord.Latest_Event`

### Vanilla behavior

`Event_Overlord.Latest_Event` is the pacing clock used to throttle random events:

```csharp
(staticVars.dateTime - Latest_Event).TotalDays
```

Vanilla refuses new events before 14 days and changes probability as elapsed time increases.

See `Event_Overlord.cs`, around lines 9-12 and 50-62.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`SaveFunction()` is empty and `LoadFunction()` calls `Reset()`, which sets:

```csharp
Latest_Event = staticVars.StartDate;
```

See `Event_Overlord.cs`, around lines 213-216 and 344-352.

### Why history is not always an exact substitute

`Set_Event()` is called from multiple routes, including dialogue activation paths. A historical “substory queued” or “random event started” timestamp does not necessarily equal every exact mutation of this pacing clock.

### IMDataCore relevance

IMDataCore captures related event/substory history but has no exact `Latest_Event` scheduler value.

Under the clarified scope, this is **not a core IMDataCore persistence requirement**. The clock is technical vanilla scheduler state. IMDC may record the actual events that occur without becoming responsible for preserving the scheduler's private pacing variable.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** no built-in scheduler checkpoint is required solely for ledger completeness.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** Area #3 Pass D finalizes one exact repair-owned `latest_event_game_date` for repaired saves, restored after `Event_Overlord.LoadFunction()` resets the field. For a pre-fix save with no repair value, use the target save game date as the deterministic conservative compatibility anchor rather than guessing an earlier event occurrence.

---

## 9. `agency._room.girl_paused`

### Vanilla behavior

Production can interrupt training:

```csharp
this.girl_paused = this.girl;
this.FinishPractice(false);
```

`FinishPractice(false)` clears the normal `girl`/room association. Later `ResumeTraining()` uses only `girl_paused` to reassign the displaced idol.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`RoomData` serializes `girl`, not `girl_paused`.

During the interrupted production state, `girl` is already null, so there is no authoritative saved association from which to infer the displaced idol.

### IMDataCore relevance

No `PauseTraining`/`girl_paused` sidecar state is persisted.

Under the clarified scope, this is **not an IMDataCore ledger gap**. It is a vanilla interrupted-state save bug. The room-generation identity that IMDC already maintains for historical correlation does not imply responsibility for mirroring every hidden room runtime field.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** no built-in persistence change is required.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** persist the displaced idol identity alongside the interrupted room state so vanilla can resume training correctly after load.

---

## 10. `agency._room.business_minutes_before_finish`

### Vanilla behavior

When production interrupts business work, `PauseBusinessProposal()` stores:

```csharp
this.business_minutes_before_finish =
    (float)(this.finishTime - staticVars.dateTime).TotalMinutes;
```

Production then overwrites the room's normal start/finish/duration/progress timer state. When business work starts again, vanilla uses the hidden remaining-minutes field.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`RoomData` does not serialize `business_minutes_before_finish` even though the field exists on `_room` (`agency.cs`, around line 3819).

Once the old business timer has been overwritten by production, the exact value cannot be reverse-calculated from the current room fields.

### IMDataCore relevance

No supplemental capture exists.

Under the clarified scope, this is **not an IMDataCore ledger gap**. The value is hidden runtime continuation state for vanilla's room scheduler.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** no built-in persistence change is required.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** persist the remaining minutes in vanilla-compatible room state and preserve vanilla's existing semantics, including that it appears to carry the *remaining amount of business work* rather than necessarily the same proposal type.

## 11. Unity RNG state

### Vanilla behavior

Idol Manager uses `UnityEngine.Random` throughout simulation for, among many other things:

- relationship dynamics,
- auditions,
- random-event choice,
- event actor and contract choice,
- concert cards,
- marketing outcomes,
- task generation,
- show calculations,
- wishes,
- assorted simulation decisions.

### Persistence hole

Neither vanilla nor IMDataCore persists `UnityEngine.Random.state`.

### Consequence

A save/load checkpoint cannot reproduce the same future stochastic trajectory even if every currently materialized gameplay datum is restored.

### Classification

This is a **deterministic-replay/design limitation**, not an IMDataCore persistence gap. IMDataCore 3.4.7 is persistence/history infrastructure, not a deterministic simulation engine.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** do not persist global Unity RNG state as part of ordinary ledger operation.

Only a separate deterministic-replay/debugging project should consider owning RNG state, and it would need compatibility rules for other mods that also consume Unity RNG.

---

## 12. Tutorial performance/promotion baselines

### Vanilla behavior

Two tutorial requirements use private static baseline counters:

```csharp
private static int performance_counter = -1;
private static int promotion_counter = -1;
```

When a corresponding requirement is first checked, vanilla snapshots the current cumulative activity count and waits for it to increase.

See `Tutorial_Reqs.cs`, around lines 32-39, 347-354, and 680-690.

### Vanilla persistence hole

`Tutorial.SaveFunction()` persists `Tutorial.Save_Data`, but `Tutorial.LoadFunction()` calls `Tutorial.Reset()`, and `Tutorial.Reset()` calls `Tutorial_Reqs.Reset()`, which resets both baselines to `-1` (`Tutorial.cs`, around lines 199-246).

If the player saves after a baseline was established but before completing the required activity, a reload can establish a new baseline and alter the intended tutorial progression condition.

### IMDataCore relevance

No tutorial baseline capture exists.

This is a **vanilla tutorial-state bug, not an IMDataCore ledger deficiency**. The counters are technical requirement-progress baselines, not useful historical diary/state data in their own right.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** no built-in persistence change is required.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** Area #3 Pass D finalizes two nullable repair-owned baselines, `performance_baseline` and `promotion_baseline`, restored after vanilla tutorial reset. Null means vanilla `-1` / not yet initialized. A pre-fix save with no repair state should remain uninitialized so the first post-migration check seeds from the target save's aggregate counter instead of inventing a historical baseline.

---

## 13. Pending delayed ambient `Scenes` assignment

### Vanilla behavior

Ambient scenes select a room/type/idol set and then schedule a delayed assignment:

```csharp
DateTime startTime = staticVars.dateTime.AddHours(UnityEngine.Random.Range(0, 20));
StartCoroutine(AssignSceneWithDelay(startTime, room, type, list));
```

The coroutine waits until the selected game time, then calls:

```csharp
room.assign(randType, usedGirls);
```

See `Scenes.cs`, around lines 350-364 and coroutine body around lines 595-614.

### Vanilla persistence hole

The pending coroutine state is not serialized. The exact already-selected:

- start time,
- room,
- scene type,
- idol list

can therefore vanish on load before assignment occurs.

Because the selection already consumed randomness, a future regeneration is not guaranteed to produce the same pending scene.

### IMDataCore relevance

No semantic capture exists for the pending `AssignSceneWithDelay` coroutine state.

Under the clarified scope, that pending coroutine is **not a core IMDataCore persistence requirement**. IMDC may reasonably record a scene when it actually occurs if that is useful history, but it should not mirror a pending coroutine closure merely to repair vanilla continuation.

### Recommended changes

**IMDataCore:** no built-in pending-job snapshot is required. If scene history is useful to consumers, capture the semantic scene assignment/presentation event when it happens.

**Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** persist each pending ambient scene semantically as due game time + scene type + stable idol IDs + a structural room locator, then reschedule it after the loaded agency/rooms are ready. Do not store the runtime room object or transient room `id`; the supplied room save shape reconstructs rooms structurally, so the repair should resolve the loaded room from stable floor/room position plus an expected room-type witness. The F9 load epoch must invalidate the discarded job before target-save rebinding.

---

## 14. Audition candidate slate and rejected outcomes

### Vanilla lifecycle

`Auditions.GenerateAudition(...)` opens/resets the popup, then starts `GenerateAudition_Delay`.

The coroutine waits `0.5f` seconds and only then calls `GenerateGirls(_data)`. See `Auditions.cs`, around lines 44-72 and 845-863.

`GenerateGirls()` creates the full randomized candidate slate with generated idol identity, rarity, stats/potentials, trait/body/texture choices, and related data.

### IMDataCore lifecycle asymmetry

IMDataCore's semantic `Auditions.GenerateAudition` capture occurs around the outer method. Its `audition_started` payload contains `generated_candidate_count`, but at the normal postfix timing `_data.Girls` has not yet been populated.

The separate `TrackAuditionGeneration()` in `Capture.RoomWork.cs` is staff-attribution bookkeeping. It does not serialize the generated candidate slate.

IMDataCore tracks hired candidates through `Audition_Data_Card.Hire`, but there is no candidate-generated or audition-completed results event that snapshots all candidates.

### Information loss

Rejected candidates are destroyed/abandoned when the audition closes. Afterwards, history may tell you that an audition happened and which candidate became a normal idol, but not:

- who all generated candidates were,
- their rarity/stats/traits,
- which candidates were rejected.

### Classification

**Clear IMDataCore historical-data gap.** It does not affect future simulation after the audition is over, but it is exactly the kind of historical lifecycle detail IMDataCore is designed to preserve.

### Recommended fix

Add:

- `audition_started`,
- `audition_candidates_generated`,
- `audition_completed`.

Each generated candidate should receive a temporary audition-scoped candidate ID. Preserve a **consumer-useful candidate summary**, not a dump of every generation/internal texture field. Useful history can include generated display identity, rarity, relevant visible stats/potentials, and:

- `hired = true/false`,
- resulting persistent idol ID if hired.

Move or repeat `generated_candidate_count` at the post-generation point.

**Area #9 Pass-C timing verdict:** the current `audition_started.generated_candidate_count` is truthfully a **start-boundary count**, and in the normal asynchronous path it is sampled before `GenerateAudition_Delay` waits 0.5 seconds and calls `GenerateGirls(...)`. Do not relabel that start-time zero as a final/generated count. Keep `audition_started` focused on the committed start/cost/cooldown state, and put the authoritative slate size plus candidate summaries on `audition_candidates_generated` after `GenerateGirls(...)` has completed. This timing issue is part of existing finding #14, not a second finding.

---

## 15. Declined business-offer details

### Vanilla lifecycle

A business proposal contains richly generated data such as:

- type,
- candidate girl set and selected girl,
- skill/image/audience,
- stamina,
- payment,
- buzz/fans/fame,
- duration,
- agent/product/description,
- staffer,
- negotiation result/coefficient/attempts.

Accepted proposals get durable consequences/history and IMDataCore captures the pre-mutation proposal snapshot through its `business.Accept` Harmony patch.

### Decline asymmetry

Vanilla `business.Decline()` mostly applies the sexy-proposal declined counter where relevant and closes the popup. It does not append the proposal details to vanilla business history.

The current IMDataCore contract patch set has a patch for `business.Accept` but no corresponding `business.Decline` capture.

### Information loss

Once declined, the exact offer disappears. Even the sexy-proposal cumulative counter cannot identify which offer caused which increment, and non-sexy declined proposals may leave no meaningful breadcrumb at all.

### Classification

**Clear IMDataCore historical-data gap.** It is not a save/load bug in the strict sense, but it is missing historical lifecycle information in a domain IMDC already models deeply.

### Recommended fix

Prefer a symmetric proposal lifecycle:

- `business_proposal_generated`,
- `business_proposal_accepted`,
- `business_proposal_declined`.

At minimum, patch `business.Decline()` and serialize the full pre-decline proposal snapshot.

---

## 16. Accepted business-proposal occurrence context (candidate slate + negotiation history)

### Vanilla generation

`business.GenerateProposal(...)` builds an offer-level candidate slate before the player chooses who should take the job. When more than three idols are active, vanilla may first add one or two pushed idols and then fills the slate to three distinct candidates with `ExtensionMethods.GetRandomElement(activeGirls)` plus a `Contains(...)` uniqueness check (`business.cs`, around lines 303-352).

The initial selected idol is simply:

```csharp
proposal.girl = proposal.Girls[0];
```

The player may later change the selected idol with `business.SelectGirl(...)`, but `proposal.Girls` remains the original candidate slate.

### The candidate set is not merely presentation data

For a sexy proposal, `business.Accept()` uses the **entire** candidate slate after the player selects one idol. Vanilla resets/halves the chosen idol's prior declined-sexy counter, then increments `Sexy_Proposals_Declined` for every other idol in `ActiveProposal.Girls` (`business.cs`, around lines 479-500).

Therefore the randomly constructed candidate set can produce authoritative gameplay mutations even on the accepted branch. It is not equivalent to a list of decorative popup options.

### Vanilla historical loss

Vanilla's accepted `business._history` row keeps only:

- proposal type,
- acceptance date,
- selected idol,
- money.

A continuing `active_proposal` likewise keeps the selected `Girl` and contract terms, not the original `Girls` candidate list. After the proposal popup closes or another proposal replaces `ActiveProposal`, the exact accepted-offer candidate slate is no longer durably represented.

The slate is not reconstructible from the later `Sexy_Proposals_Declined` counters. Those counters are cumulative, may be changed by declined proposals too, and do not encode which acceptance occurrence changed which idols. For non-sexy accepted offers there may be no candidate-side breadcrumb at all.

### IMDataCore has the exact data and discards it

This is a particularly clean IMDataCore-domain omission because the existing Harmony patch is already on the correct side of the mutation.

`business_Accept_IMDataCoreCapture_Patch` runs a prefix and calls `CreateContractAcceptedSnapshot(...)`. That method clones `ActiveProposal` **before** vanilla acceptance runs (`IMDataCoreController.Capture.SinglesGroups.cs`, around lines 1473-1490). The clone therefore still exposes the full `proposal.Girls` candidate list.

However, IMDataCore then calls `ResolveProposalTargetIdolIdentifiers(...)`, whose implementation intentionally emits only `proposal.girl`. Its comment says the other `Girls` entries are UI candidates that did not participate in the accepted contract (`IMDataCore.cs`, around lines 3461-3478).

That comment is semantically too strong for vanilla behavior: on sexy acceptance, the unselected candidates do participate in the acceptance mutation through `Sexy_Proposals_Declined`.

`BuildContractLifecyclePayloadFromProposal(...)` serializes the selected idol's contract terms, agent/product, duration, and related fields, but contains no ordered proposal-candidate ID list.

### Area #4 closure revalidation: accepted negotiation history also belongs here

The closure revalidation followed the Pass-B negotiation branch back through `business.Negotiations()`. Each attempt increments `ActiveProposal.negotiation_attempts`, stores the latest Boolean `negotiation` result, and changes `negotiationCoeff`. `CreateContractAcceptedSnapshot(...)` clones the live `_proposal` before `Accept()` mutates/discards proposal-only context, so IMDataCore already has the authoritative candidate slate **and** the final negotiation occurrence state at the correct capture point.

IMDataCore's money-ledger detail layer partially preserves negotiation context: proposal/contract metadata can expose the effective multiplier and `negotiation_attempts`. That is useful, but it is not a substitute for the semantic proposal timeline. The accepted contract lifecycle payload still lacks the ordered candidate slate, the final `negotiation` success/failure state, the raw `negotiationCoeff`, and a proposal occurrence identity linking generation, negotiation, acceptance/decline, and any continuing contract instance.

The closure revalidation therefore **does not create a new numbered finding**. It strengthens #16 from “candidate slate only” to the broader **accepted proposal occurrence context** already implied by this section's recommended proposal lifecycle.

### Classification

**Clear IMDataCore historical-completeness gap.** This is a historical-only vanilla omission rather than a save/load continuation bug. It is nevertheless an irretrievable generated gameplay fact in a business lifecycle IMDataCore already models, and its pre-accept prefix already has the authoritative list available.

### Recommended fix

Prefer a proposal-level lifecycle distinct from the later active-contract lifecycle:

- `business_proposal_generated`
- `business_proposal_accepted`
- `business_proposal_declined`

Give each generated offer a proposal occurrence ID, for example `p:<guid>`, and carry at least:

- ordered `candidate_idol_id_list`,
- `selected_idol_id`,
- proposal type/skill,
- agent/product,
- payment/buzz/fans/fame/stamina/duration,
- negotiation result/coefficient/attempts,
- generation and terminal dates.

At minimum, enrich the existing `contract_accepted` capture with the ordered candidate ID list from the prefix snapshot. The proposal occurrence ID is preferable because it can also unify finding #15's declined-offer history and later correlate the accepted proposal to the durable `contract_instance_id` when a continuing contract is created.

**Cross-tag:** Audit Area #9 should also revisit the misleading `ResolveProposalTargetIdolIdentifiers(...)` comment/semantics, because the current implementation describes unselected candidates as nonparticipants even though vanilla mutates them for sexy offers.

**Area #8 Pass-B lifecycle revalidation:** the current `contract_window_opened` name does **not** fill the missing proposal-birth endpoint. `CaptureContractActivated(...)` emits `contract_window_opened` from the `business.AddActiveProposal(...)` activation path using an active-contract payload. It therefore occurs only after a continuing proposal has already been accepted/converted into an active contract; declined proposals and accepted zero-duration proposals never receive that row. Treat this as an **Area #9 semantic naming/timing cross-tag**, while #15/#16 continue to own the missing proposal-level `generated -> accepted/declined` lifecycle/history requirement.

---

## 17. Idol hire-time generated profile / initial parameter baseline + hire provenance

### Generated composite

`data_girls.GenerateGirl(...)` constructs a new idol from many independent generated pieces before the idol is hired (`data_girls.cs`, around lines 244-331):

- a new vanilla idol ID;
- generated first/last name;
- generated sexuality;
- generated trait;
- generated birthday and peak age;
- generated portrait/body assets, which can override name, rarity, trait, age, and stat presets;
- the full parameter set, including generated starting values and potentials.

The dead/vestigial `girls.popularity` roll is deliberately **not** part of this finding. Pass A already rejected it as a meaningful persistence target.

All ordinary generated-idol acquisition paths eventually converge on `data_girls.Hire(...)`, including audition cards, graduation-successor recruitment, and unique/story recruits. `Hire(...)` stamps `Hiring_Date`, creates relationships, inserts the idol into the live roster, and fires the hired lifecycle.

### Vanilla continuation is correct

This is **not** a Save n Load Fixes finding. `data_girls.SaveFunction()` serializes the live idol's parameters, ID, birthday, names, nickname, sexuality, trait, type, hiring date, portrait asset references, and the other state needed to reconstruct the current idol. Vanilla can therefore resume the current idol correctly.

The historical problem is different: as training, aging, story actions, injuries, policies, and other systems change the idol, the original hire-time parameter values are overwritten. Vanilla does not retain a durable “this is who she was when hired” snapshot.

### IMDataCore captures the hire at the right time, but the payload is too thin

IMDataCore patches `data_girls.Hire(...)` with a Prefix/Postfix (`Patches/Systems/SystemEventPatches.cs`, around lines 1240-1262). The Postfix calls `CaptureIdolHired(...)` only after proving the idol was actually inserted. That is an excellent authoritative capture point.

However, `BuildIdolLifecyclePayload(...)` (`IMDataCore.cs`, around lines 4009-4047) currently emits:

- idol ID;
- lifecycle action/status;
- idol type and age;
- hiring/graduation dates;
- graduation outcome/trivia;
- portrait identity;
- staff attribution.

`IdolLifecyclePayload` (`IMDataCore.cs`, around lines 7970-7998) has no fields for the idol's name, exact birthday, sexuality, trait, or initial parameter values/potentials. The generic `LightweightEventRecord` envelope likewise carries `IdolId`, entity/event identity, dates, source patch, and payload JSON rather than a separate idol-name snapshot.

A downstream diary can often resolve a **current** idol by ID, but that is not equivalent to the hire-time composite. The initial stat/potential baseline is especially non-reconstructible after the idol changes, and a self-contained historical event is also more robust when later deletion/history-resolvability work is considered.

### Classification

- **Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** No separate vanilla bug is identified in this finding; vanilla current-state persistence for the idol is adequate.
- **IMDataCore:** **YES, historical/backend coverage gap.** A hire milestone is already a first-class IMDataCore event, and a compact initial profile is a natural semantic baseline for diary/history consumers rather than a raw technical dump.

### Recommended IMDataCore fix

Enrich `idol_hired` at the existing Postfix capture point. Preserve semantic generated facts, not RNG internals:

- `idol_first_name`, `idol_last_name`, `idol_nickname` or a stable display-name snapshot;
- exact `idol_birthday`;
- `idol_sexuality`;
- `idol_trait`;
- existing idol type and portrait identity;
- compact initial core-parameter baseline with **value + potential** for the stable idol parameters.

An ordered `idol_initial_parameters` array or stable parameter-code map is preferable to eight ad-hoc field pairs. Do not add `girls.popularity`, raw RNG rolls, or unrelated mutable runtime internals.

**Area #9 Pass-B reconciliation:** hire-source/provenance is folded into this existing finding rather than counted again. The current `idol_hired` source is always the `data_girls.Hire` patch, so enrich the same historical event with a stable `idol_hire_source` / optional detail code that distinguishes at least audition, graduation successor, unique/story recruit, and other/mod-driven `Hire(...)` routes where source evidence exists. This is historical provenance only; it is not current-state persistence.

## 18. Generic player-date occurrence details are captured before the date composite exists

### Vanilla date flow

`Date_Popup.OnClick_GoDate()` first calls `Dating.GoOnDate(Girl)`. For an ordinary repeatable date, `GoOnDate()` returns the token `"generic"` (`Dating.cs`, around lines 267-346).

Only **after that method has returned** does the popup establish the actual date occurrence:

1. `OnClick_GoDateLocation(...)` either accepts the player's chosen location or calls `Dating.GetRandomDatingLocation(...)`;
2. it writes the authoritative location through `Dating.SetNextLocation(...)`;
3. the player chooses whether to wear masks;
4. `Dating.SetMasks(...)` writes that choice;
5. `Dating.GenerateGenericDate(...)` builds the actual dialogue occurrence.

`GenerateGenericDate(...)` then chooses a fresh location-appropriate question when possible, builds the location/music/actors/script, inserts the question/outro, and adds the final dating-points effect (`Dating.cs`, around lines 565-645).

### Vanilla retains only coarse date history

`data_girls.girls._date_history` contains only `MeetingDate` and broad `Type`. `data_girls.SaveFunction()` serializes exactly those two fields for date history. It does not retain the generic date's aquarium/arcade/bookstore/park/mall location, mask choice, or generated question occurrence.

That is acceptable for vanilla continuation after a completed date. It is therefore **not** a Save n Load Fixes finding under the ordinary legal-save-boundary test.

### IMDataCore capture is on the wrong side of the composite generation

IMDataCore patches `Dating.GoOnDate(...)` and emits `player_date_interaction` in a Postfix (`PushAndRelationshipPatches.cs`, around lines 347-366). `CapturePlayerDateInteraction(...)` records route/stage/status before/after, the returned result token/summary, caught state, romance level before/after, and producer attribution.

For the generic path, that Postfix executes **before** the location and mask choices and before `GenerateGenericDate(...)` constructs the occurrence. `PlayerDateInteractionPayload` consequently has no generic-date location, mask choice, or question/dialogue occurrence identifier.

That leaves a conspicuous diary gap. IMDataCore can say roughly “the player initiated a generic date with idol #17,” but not the natural historical fact “the player went to the aquarium with idol #17.” The location is not reliably inferable later from vanilla `DateHistory`; exhausted location-specific questions can fall back to generic questions/small talk, so used-dialogue history is not a dependable reconstruction route either.

### Area #9 Pass-C timing verdict

The same capture boundary makes the current generic-date `*_after` fields **provably pre-completion snapshots**, not merely suspicious ones. On the generic branch, `Dating.GoOnDate()` returns the token `"generic"`; only afterward does `Date_Popup` collect the location/mask choices, call `Dating.GenerateGenericDate(...)`, and build the dialogue whose final node carries the `dating/add_points` effect. IMDataCore's `Dating.GoOnDate` Postfix therefore samples `DateRouteAfter`, `DateStageAfter`, and especially `DateRelationshipLevelAfter` before the completed generic-date occurrence has applied its final dating mutation.

This does **not** create a second numbered finding. It broadens finding #18 from missing occurrence context to a timing contract: the existing `player_date_interaction` row may represent the **attempt/route-decision boundary**, but it must not advertise generic-date completion state as `*_after` unless those fields are renamed to attempt-time semantics. A correlated generic-date presentation/completion capture should sample final route/stage/relationship state only after the generated dialogue's semantic effects have committed.

### Classification

- **Cosmo Save n Load Fixes:** No separate vanilla bug is identified here for a normally completed date. Vanilla does not need this historical detail to continue.
- **IMDataCore:** **YES, historical/backend coverage gap.** Date location is a compact, player-facing semantic fact that a diary/history consumer can reasonably expect from an existing player-date event.

### Recommended IMDataCore fix

Do not log rendered dialogue or raw random choices. Add a Harmony capture point on the semantic occurrence, preferably `Dating.GenerateGenericDate(data_girls.girls)`, where `Dating.Next_Location` and `Dating.Wear_Masks` are already authoritative.

A minimal generic-date occurrence payload should include:

- idol ID;
- occurrence game date;
- generic date location code;
- `wear_masks`;
- optional generated question/dialogue ID when present and useful for history correlation.

The existing `player_date_interaction` may remain as an attempt/route-decision event, or IMDataCore can add correlated `player_generic_date_presented` / `player_generic_date_completed` semantic events. **Pass C finalizes the timing rule:** completion-state fields and relationship delta must be sampled after the generated dialogue's `dating/add_points` effect has actually committed, while the earlier `GoOnDate()` Postfix must use attempt/decision naming if retained.

## 19. `Date_Flirt` semantic flirt outcome history

### Vanilla behavior

The ordinary idol-interaction popup wires its flirt button directly to `Date_Popup.OnClick_Flirt()` (`Date_Popup.cs:147`, `352-360`). That method marks the broad date-history type as `flirt`, then calls:

```csharp
Date_Flirt.DoFlirt(this.Girl);
```

`Date_Flirt.DoFlirt(...)` delegates the meaningful result to `Date_Flirt.GetOutcome(...)` (`Date_Flirt.cs:35-137`, `190-254`). The helper can establish semantic outcomes including:

- `critical_success`;
- `success`;
- `failure`;
- `catastrophic_failure`;
- `wrong_gender`;
- `taken`;
- `uninterested`;
- `oblivious`;
- `too_fast`; and
- `uncomfortable`.

Those outcomes are not merely text selectors. `DoFlirt(...)` can mutate `DatingData.Success_Counter`, romance progress, friendship points, `DatingData.Previous_Attempt`, sexuality/partner-knowledge flags, `Used_Goods`, and related dating state.

### Vanilla persistence is sufficient for continuation, but not history

Vanilla persists the current `DatingData` object (`data_girls.cs:2015`, `2174`) and persists `DateHistory`, but a date-history entry contains only `MeetingDate` plus a broad `_date_history._type` such as `flirt` (`data_girls.cs:2054-2059`, `6252+`).

`DatingData.Previous_Attempt` preserves only the **latest** flirt outcome. A later flirt overwrites it. Therefore an old occurrence such as:

> critical success on March 4

or:

> flirt failed because the idol revealed she already had a partner

cannot be reconstructed later from vanilla state once subsequent interactions have changed the same fields.

This is **not** a Save n Load Fixes defect. The current gameplay state itself is saved correctly.

### IMDataCore coverage gap

The supplied IMDataCore patches `Dating.GoOnDate()` and `Dating.GoOnSpecificDate()` for `player_date_interaction`, and patches generic player-relationship point changes. It has no patch on:

- `Date_Popup.OnClick_Flirt()`;
- `Date_Flirt.DoFlirt(...)`; or
- `Date_Flirt.GetOutcome(...)`.

A friendship/romance delta is not enough to recover the semantic outcome, especially for discovery outcomes or `oblivious`/`too_fast`/`uncomfortable` branches.

The randomly selected **dialogue wording** from `Date_Flirt.GetRandomFlirt(...)` is presentation and should not be logged. The durable fact is the **outcome category and resulting semantic changes**.

### Recommended IMDataCore fix

Prefer a Harmony Prefix/Postfix on the public static semantic owner:

```text
Date_Flirt.DoFlirt(data_girls.girls)
```

rather than patching `mainScript.chance()` or the private RNG mechanics.

Capture a compact before/after snapshot and emit a semantic event such as:

```text
player_flirt_outcome
```

Suggested fields:

- `idol_id`;
- `flirt_outcome`;
- `success_counter_before`;
- `success_counter_after`;
- `romance_points_before`;
- `romance_points_after`;
- `friendship_points_before`;
- `friendship_points_after`;
- `sexuality_known_before/after`;
- `partner_status_known_before/after`;
- `used_goods_before/after`;
- `partner_status_known_to_player_before/after`;
- occurrence game date.

Do not preserve the randomly selected line IDs/text unless a later consumer requirement proves those presentation variants are independently useful.

**Classification:** IMDataCore historical/backend gap only; no separate vanilla bug requiring Save n Load Fixes was identified in this finding.
